notes:
# #88 evaluation notes (20 October)

- Fresh baseline setup (`make chartsearch-research-setup`, baseline hiv-20261019-025659) finished 20:17 UTC.
  Settings already match the 7 October run (queryScoped, grounding and drug reference off, remote
  gemma-4-12b via the router, topK 12); rate limit raised 10 -> 1000 for the run (restore afterwards).
  Router preset matches October's except `swa-full = true`.
- Cohort: the five October patients, record counts identical (320/121/168/157/214), all 7,840 gold
  record references present in the charts; frozen in universe.json.
- FINDING (QueryStore): the first per-patient reindex of the five patients, at 20:17 UTC right after setup,
  returned HTTP 200 with documentsIndexed 0 for each (about 3 s each) and deleted their documents;
  full-chart reads then returned 0 records with chartTruncated false and projectionComplete true.
  Repeating the reindex a few minutes later re-projected each patient fully (320/121/168/157/214).
  Not yet diagnosed: the per-patient HQL and the type list are correct; nothing was logged.
- QueryStore integration (-Pintegration, MySQL and Elasticsearch): #90 525f8b7 560 run, #88 tip 56360db
  626 run; the only error on both is hybridFusesBm25AndKnnViaSpiDefault, the zero-vector test bug #89 fixes.
- The reindex failure is intermittent, not limited to startup: for patient 39 the sequence was fail,
  succeed, fail, fail, fail, succeed (curl and Python alike). When it fails Elasticsearch holds no
  documents for the patient; when it succeeds the count climbs to the full 320 while the call runs.
  The runner now repeats a reindex until the reported count matches universe.json and records every attempt.
- In the #87 arm's re-projection, each patient failed three times and succeeded on the fourth attempt
  (20 s between attempts, so roughly 60-80 s after the first): a time-based cause, such as a cache entry
  expiring, is more likely than a random fault.
- Owner decisions (20 October): finish this evaluation first, then build a new default baseline with
  QueryStore #88 (full resync of the changed types), export and publish it to GHCR, commit hiv-baseline.json.
- ROOT CAUSE (20 October, 20:46 UTC): Elasticsearch keeps a tombstone for a deleted document for
  index.gc_deletes (60 s default) and rejects a versioned write at or below the tombstone's version.
  QueryStore writes with version_type=external_gte and version=last_modified; its deletes were
  unversioned (delete_by_query, bulk delete, single delete), which leaves the tombstone one above the
  document's version. reindexPatient deletes then rewrites the same records at the same last_modified,
  so every rewrite within 60 s of the delete got a 409, which countBulkSuccess counted as a "stale
  write skipped" success. Evidence: one reindex of patient 39 raised the ES index_failed counter by
  640 (320 docs on primaries and replicas) and wrote nothing; a scratch-index probe reproduced the
  conflict and showed a delete issued at the document's own external version leaves a tombstone at
  that version, after which the same-version rewrite is accepted with the version intact.
  Zero gc_deletes does not help (still a conflict). Both the delete-first reindex (463e241) and the
  409-as-success counting (689fce2) are in upstream main, so the fix is a new PR off main:
  branch codex/rewrite-after-delete in work/qs-fix-wt. The merge sweep and a void followed by an
  unvoid hit the same tombstone, so all three delete paths now delete at the document's version.
- FIX (20 October, 21:05 UTC): QueryStore PR #91 (codex/rewrite-after-delete, c3ec5a5) deletes every
  Elasticsearch document at its own external version. Red: three new integration tests failed with 0
  documents; green: the class runs 37 with the one pre-existing knn zero-vector error (#89). Unit
  suites: api 483 (2 skipped), omod 21. The #88 arm runs on codex/eval-88-rewrite-fix (d61c14d), the
  merge of #88 56360db with the fix, pushed to the fork as the arm's provenance. run_arm.py now
  reindexes once per patient and stops the run on anything but the full count.
